# API Levels

Every public declaration of a published module has one of four levels. The ABI dumps (`<module>/api/<module>.api`) record the signatures of the first three, so a change to them shows in review. The markers are in `me.ahoo.wow.api.annotation` of `wow-annotations`, which every Wow artifact but `wow-cocache-api` brings along.

| Level | Marker | Promise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | none | A 10.0.x patch release keeps it binary compatible. A 10.x minor release keeps it source compatible: a caller's sources compile unchanged and its binaries are rebuilt against it; the release notes name every signature that changed. |
| Experimental | `@ExperimentalWowApi` | A 10.x minor release may change or remove it. Using it needs `@OptIn(ExperimentalWowApi::class)`, a compiler warning otherwise. |
| SPI | `@WowSpi` | A port that backends and transports implement; a minor release may change it. Using it needs `@OptIn(WowSpi::class)`, a compiler warning otherwise. |
| Internal | `@InternalWowApi` | For Wow's own modules: it may change or go in any release. Using it without opting in is a compiler error, and an application does not opt in; the dumps leave it out. |

## Beyond the API

The API is one of three things an upgrade keeps compatible. Within a major version, adjacent minor versions run side by side: the cluster channel, the wait signals, the Kafka envelope, the log's entries and the leases stay readable by the minor version before and after ([Upgrade a Deployment](../operate/upgrades)). A service's own contract, its commands, events, state and error codes, is held to its committed baseline by the build's compatibility check ([The Manifest](../guide/manifest)). Across a major version, a service moves once, with a blue-green cut-over.

The two lists below are generated from the sources of the published modules: the public declarations that carry the marker.
